$comment: Ground truth for SECOND WORLD recall/precision on orders-jobs-api (docs/12-testing-and-quality.md §3). Same format as examples/conduit-api/expected-findings.json: location.line = the line after the SEEDED-DEFECT marker (refresh with `node examples/_tools/sync-expected-findings.mjs examples/orders-jobs-api`); detectedBy = the CLI commands that find the defect with exactly this folder's sw.config.ts (finding ruleId + operation, title fragment or location); several entries for one command are alternative rules for the same defect. `observations` = documented findings that are not defects. Checked by tests/system/orders-jobs.test.ts.

defects.title: Payment worker retries with a fixed 100 ms delay: no exponential backoff, no jitter, no circuit breaker
defects.reproduction: Make the provider answer 503: each payment job sends 8 charge attempts 100 ms apart, 4 workers in lock-step (≈5x the steady-state calls per request)
defects.fix: Exponential backoff with full jitter (delay = random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))), a retry budget and a circuit breaker per provider

defects.title: GET /orders/{id}/payment?refresh=true calls the provider without a timeout
defects.reproduction: Black-hole the provider: GET /orders/1/payment?refresh=true hangs until the provider answers again
defects.fix: fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) }) and answer from local state (provider: unavailable) on timeout

defects.title: Payment webhook is not idempotent: a redelivered event (same Idempotency-Key) is recorded and counted again
defects.reproduction: POST the same charge.succeeded event twice with Idempotency-Key evt_x: two event records (different ids), order 1 amountPaid 2500 → 7500
defects.fix: Look the key up first (or INSERT … ON CONFLICT(idempotency_key) DO NOTHING) and return the stored record; apply the payment only on the pending → paid transition

defects.title: Unbounded payment job queue: under load the API keeps accepting orders while every job waits longer
defects.reproduction: 48 checkouts+browses/s (≈24 orders/s) against ≈13 jobs/s of worker capacity: job wait p95 grows past 3 s within 6 s and keeps growing; no 503 is ever returned
defects.fix: Bound the queue (e.g. 50 jobs): answer 503 + Retry-After when it is full (load shedding), as the contract says
defects.description: Needs the job-wait SLO in performance.thresholds (endpoint.GET /jobs/{{job}}.p95 < 2000ms, measured by the checkout scenario's long-poll): latency of the HTTP API alone does not show a growing backlog.

defects.title: Stale read after update: PUT /orders/{id} does not invalidate the order read cache
defects.reproduction: GET /orders/1 (cached), PUT /orders/1 { note: 'new' } → 200, GET /orders/1 → old note (for up to 30 s)
defects.fix: cache.delete(`${user.id}:${id}`) after the UPDATE (as DELETE does), or write the new view through
defects.description: Found by the register-model concurrency test in bugs.concurrency (read → updates → read), by the bugs model-based stateful technique (create → read → update → read) and by sw agent's lifecycle probe (create → read → update → read), since the wave-8 fixes in those engines.

observations.reason: Per-run experiment summary (info). Not a defect.
